title: The story of the teddy bear
text:
The teddy bear owes its name to an American president, who in 1902 went hunting in Mississippi {A}. According to the story, his assistants caught a small bear and tied it to a tree {B}, but he refused to shoot an animal that could not defend itself. A cartoon of the scene appeared in a newspaper, and a shopkeeper in Brooklyn, {C}, made a soft toy bear and asked permission to call it 'Teddy's bear'.

At almost the same time, a German company was developing its own version. The toy was stuffed with straw and had movable arms and legs, {D}. It was shown at a trade fair in 1903, where an American buyer ordered thousands.

Today the bear is not only a children's plaything. Collectors pay high prices for old examples, {E} as evidence of changing tastes. Many adults admit that they still own the toy {F}, and few of them can explain why.
